## What this is

This is a working pack, not a book. Nothing in it needs reading cover to
cover. It is a set of artefacts you can put in front of a team on Monday:
prompts to paste, a policy to adapt, a plan to follow, a scoring sheet to
argue over, and a list of the places where the honest answer is to close
the laptop.

It was written by a chartered accountant, for people whose name goes on
the work.

## What it deliberately does not contain

No statistics about AI adoption. No productivity percentages. No case
studies about firms that saved a fortune. No promises about your income
or your job.

Everything in that list is standard in this market and almost none of it
is checkable. The moment a pack like this quotes a figure nobody can
verify, every other claim in it becomes a guess too. So there are no
numbers here except the ones you generate yourself, in your own team,
measuring your own work.

What that costs you: this pack cannot tell you what results to expect.
What it buys you: everything it does tell you can be checked.

## How to use it

**If you have not started at all.** Read *Choosing What to Automate
First*, run the 45-minute meeting at the end of it, and pick two use
cases. Two, not ten. Then take the policy from *Your Policy Documents*,
fill it in, and circulate it before anyone else starts experimenting.
That order matters — a policy written after the tools have spread is a
document about a problem you already have.

**If your team is already using AI without rules.** Start with *Your
Policy Documents* today. Then *Verification, Red Lines and Choosing a
Tool*. The prompts can wait a fortnight; the red lines cannot.

**If you are the one who has to teach it.** Go to the four-level
curriculum in *The 90-Day Adoption Plan and the Training Curriculum*.
Each level is written so you can teach it without outside help, with the
live exercise already specified.

**If you just want better output tomorrow morning.** *The Prompt Library*.
Find the workflow that matches what is on your desk, adapt the prompt
rather than pasting it blind, and read the check line underneath it
before you use anything it gives you.

## The one rule underneath all of it

Whoever signs the work owns the work.

A tool is never the reason something went out wrong. Every prompt in this
pack has a line under it telling you what to check, because a fluent
answer and a correct answer look identical until you look. That is the
whole discipline. The rest is technique.

## A note on what is general and what is yours

Everything here that touches law, tax, professional standards or
regulatory duty is general information. Rules differ between countries
and professions, and they change. No document in this pack is legal
advice, and adopting any of it is not a statement that you comply with
anything. Have the policy read by whoever carries risk in your
organisation, and check it against your own regulator's guidance and your
client engagement terms before you use it.
